messages:
alice: thinking out loud — the recent spike in spot interruptions killed a bunch of interactive sessions. proposal: introduce an "eviction credit" smoothing layer per-queue. each interactive session gets X credits that decay slowly; a preempt event consumes credits first instead of immediate eviction. credits top up on steady-state time. this would let short bursts of churn not kick users immediately, while still letting us reclaim nodes for batch when credits are exhausted. what do folks think?

ben: curious — how do you pick X? and what's the failure mode if credits accumulate and we starve batch?

alice: good q. idea is to make X proportional to queue SLA and historical churn for the instance type. interactive queues get higher refill rates, batch queues lower. also add a hard cap so credits can't block needed reclaim for >N seconds. default X=30s equivalent for p99 interactive response as a starting point.

carla: love the smoothing idea. we should combine it with provider preemption notices where available (GCE 30s/EC2 2-minute spot-fleet signals). use the window to checkpoint KV caches and opportunistically migrate lightweight sessions to hot-pool nodes. also: measure how often credits actually save us vs. just deferring evictions.

danny: note that eu-west has a NIC shortage next week (net quota bump delayed). if we hold onto instances with credits, we might exacerbate cross-region imbalance. we should allow forced preempt for region-balancing with a different metric that ignores credits when global capacity delta > threshold.

emma: proposed k8s implementation sketch: use a small admission controller that annotates pods with eviction_credit=<seconds>. node controller evaluates credits during scale-down/eviction decisions. also use priorityClass for interactive (p100-interactive) + taints for batch-hot-preempt to prefer reclaiming batch.

ben: can you paste a minimal mutating webhook patch?

carla: here's a tiny example we tried in test:

```
# mutating webhook pseudo-patch
kubectl patch pod $POD -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"eviction_credit":"30"}}}'
```

and node controller pseudo-check: if node.pressure && pod.eviction_credit>0 then decrement and skip eviction else evict.

infra-bot: weekly-spot-summary: last week interrupted_instances=1123, avg_interruption_window=42s, p95_restarts=1.7, interactive_evictions_up_24% :rotating_light: (see /incidents/1844309000)

alice: ok so action items I see: 1) carla to run sim with X={15,30,60} and report impact on batch throughput and interactive tail latency. 2) danny to add cross-region forced-preempt threshold to the plan. 3) emma to draft the mutating webhook + node controller checklist for canary deploy. 4) ben to model cost delta if we keep credits at scale (estimated % of time nodes are held).

carla: I can run sims today on perf-cluster-qa. I'll include a synthetic churn trace (copy of last week's) and measure batch backlog growth.

danny: I'll pull region capacity projections and produce a simple decision rule: if region_available_capacity < 5% then ignore credits for top-k nodes. will post numbers here.

emma: for the canary, let's run on a 5% subset of interactive traffic and watch p99 latency for 48h. if tail latency improves (or at least doesn't regress) and batch backlog delta < 3%, we graduate. :thumbsup:

alice: sounds good — thanks everyone. tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
